title: RESEARCH: size_t→word32 silent truncation in flash_sign/verify/decrypt
description: src/wp11_backend_usb_flash.c: wc_RsaSSL_Sign, wc_RsaPrivateDecrypt, wc_RsaSSL_Verify all receive size_t lengths cast to word32 (uint32_t). On 64-bit platforms where size_t=64bit and word32=32bit, a buffer >4GB would silently truncate. RSA buffers are never 4GB in practice. However: wc_RsaSSL_Verify writes up to keysize bytes into the 512-byte stack buffer 'out'. Research: verify wolfCrypt's wc_RsaSSL_Verify internal behavior — does it check that the output fits in outlen BEFORE writing, or does it compute the output size from the key and write regardless? If it writes key_size bytes unconditionally, a 4096-bit key (512 bytes) will exactly fill the 512-byte buffer but a 4097-bit hypothetical key would overflow. Add inline comment at the stack buffer documenting the assumption: RSA-4096 max = 512 bytes. Reject keys larger than 4096 bits in wp11_keystore_create or document the limitation.
